ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Predominantly low-intensity (black) pixels covering approximately 85% of the visible surface, with high-intensity (white) pixels concentrated in the upper 15% along the trailing edge.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: A solid black primary region occupies the central and lower portions of the fluke. High-contrast white pigmentation appears as a thick, irregular horizontal band along the trailing edge of the left lobe and as fragmented, mottled patches along the trailing edge of the right lobe.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: A sharp, symmetrical V-shaped indentation with a vertex angle of approximately 65 degrees and a vertical depth roughly 1/5th of the total fluke height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular serrations with pixel amplitudes ranging from 2 to 10 pixels. The right lobe shows more pronounced, jagged peaks, while the left lobe displays a slightly smoother, though still irregular, jagged profile.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: The trailing edges of both lobes follow a strongly convex trajectory from the median notch to the distal tips, characterized by a distinct outward-curving arc.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Prominent clusters of high-contrast white pixels at the extreme distal tips of both lobes, indicating dense barnacle colonization. Several circular, low-contrast 'ghost' rosettes are visible on the dark pigmented area of the right mid-lobe.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: A series of roughly vertical, high-intensity linear marks (scratches) are detected on the dark central pigmentation, particularly concentrated near the vertical axis above the peduncle.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extensive barnacle colonization at the tips of both lobes; visible vertical linear rake marks or scratches on the central lower fluke.
other_distinctive_markers: Visible water droplets shedding from the trailing edge create a series of high-intensity vertical point-trails below the fluke profile.
